newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING says Barings lifts income, costs.
newsitem.headline: ING says Barings lifts income, costs.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV (ING) said the London-based Barings investment bank contributed to an increase in commission income and operating expenditure in the first nine months of 1996.
The group earlier announced a 24 percent jump in net profit to 2.34 billion guilders for the period.
Commission income grew 35.1 percent to 1.98 billion.

"In addition to the influence of Barings, this was due to higher commission income recorded by the other banking operations from securities and corporate finance and higher fees for asset management," ING said.

ING bought Barings last year for 1.7 billion guilders after the investment bank collapsed from huge derivatives trading losses, and the Dutch group has since folded it into its investment banking unit, now called ING Barings.
Operating expenditure of the banking operations rose 22.5 percent to 6.04 billion guilders for the same period.

"In addition to the expansion of the international banking operations, this increase was mainly due the acquisition of Barings and provisions amounting to NLG 125 million for information technology, the introduction of the euro and the year 2000," ING said.
